name: Email delivery and preferences
summary: Who receives platform emails, how notification preferences filter them, retries, and the delivery audit trail.

roles.note: Each user manages their own notification preferences per project. Sending is done by services, not by users.

nfr.statement: How long email audit records are kept, and who may read them.

requirements.title: Recipients are resolved to users, and test environments don't email customers
requirements.statement: An email needs a template and recipients. Addresses that belong to known users are resolved to those users; other addresses are kept as raw emails. Outside production and beta, known users from outside Track3D's own domains are skipped. Some company-and-template pairs can also be blocked.
open_checks: Raw unmatched addresses skip the environment filter that applies to known users

acceptance_criteria.given: The dev environment, and an email to a customer user at acme.com

requirements.title: Notification preferences filter recipients
requirements.statement: If a user has no preference set for the project, they receive the email. If they do, the email's notification category (or the type's default) must be enabled. Recipients are de-duplicated before sending.
open_checks: An unknown notification type can suppress delivery for users who have preferences

acceptance_criteria.given: A user who turned off alert emails for project P
acceptance_criteria.when: An alert email for P is sent to them and two others
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the other two receive it, once each

requirements.title: Sending retries up to three times and is audited
requirements.statement: Each email is tried up to 3 times. Its start, success or error is saved in an email audit record.

acceptance_criteria.given: The email provider fails twice and then succeeds
acceptance_criteria.then: It is delivered, and its audit record shows success
